permissions.name: Azure role assignment write ('Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write', and '.../delete' for deployment delete: Owner, User Access Administrator or Role Based Access Control Administrator) at scope '/subscriptions/6e1f4c2a-0000-4000-8000-000000000003'
reasons: provider: PUT {scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/{guid} (deployment delete: DELETE; whatif reads roleAssignments: '.../read', for example Reader)

permissions.name: Azure role eligibility request ('Microsoft.Authorization/roleEligibilityScheduleRequests/write': Owner or User Access Administrator) at scope '/subscriptions/6e1f4c2a-0000-4000-8000-000000000003'
reasons: provider: PUT {scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleEligibilityScheduleRequests/{guid} (AdminAssign; deployment delete AdminRemove; whatif reads roleEligibilitySchedules: '.../read', for example Reader)

permissions.name: Azure role management policy write ('Microsoft.Authorization/roleManagementPolicies/write': Owner, User Access Administrator or Role Based Access Control Administrator) at scope '/subscriptions/6e1f4c2a-0000-4000-8000-000000000003'
reasons: provider: PATCH {scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleManagementPolicies/{policy} (whatif reads it: '.../read', for example Reader)

notes: Application permissions are Microsoft Graph app roles granted (with admin consent) to the service principal EARM signs in with (AZURE_CLIENT_ID, or the managed identity). Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy replaces Application.ReadWrite.All for applications the service principal owns.

Optional, not listed above: User.ReadBasic.All (or a broader user or directory read such as User.Read.All or Directory.Read.All) lets every online run read the tenant size right after the preflight (GET /users/$count) and pace Graph requests with the tenant's directory budget; without it the run goes on with the smallest tenant's budget (3,500 resource units per 10 s), which only makes a large deployment slower.

Azure role management policies (Microsoft.Entra/azureRoleManagementPolicies) are read and written through Azure Resource Manager with its own token: the signed-in identity needs the Azure RBAC grant listed at each policy's scope (no Graph permission), and a delegated sign-in the one-time Resource Manager consent (earm auth login -f <template>).

Azure role grants (Microsoft.Entra/azureRoleAssignments, Microsoft.Entra/azureRoleEligibilityScheduleRequests) are read and written through Azure Resource Manager with its own token: the signed-in identity needs the Azure RBAC grant listed at each declared scope (no Graph permission), and a delegated sign-in the one-time Resource Manager consent (earm auth login -f <template>).

Edge permissions are listed for every relationship property the template declares (including an empty array, which removes edges). Key Vault access is an Azure RBAC / access-policy requirement of the signed-in identity, not a Graph permission.
